text:
matt d: Quick heads-up — planning sync for console observability launch readiness. Need to lock canary criteria, final MVP dashboards, tracing hooks, and the per-route cost surface. Beta customers already asked for finance breakdowns and better error slices.

anya: Thx — summary of an MVP proposal: 1) Dashboards: overview (latency/cost/error trend), model-cost by route, and long-tail errors (top 10 error signatures). 2) Tracing: inject trace_id into infra logs, span for model selection + backend fallback. 3) Cost: per-route token cost + percent of total. 4) Launch criteria: canary stability for 72h, P95 latency within +10% of baseline, error delta <0.5pp.

sofia: I like that. Implementation notes: tracing hooks will take ~2 sprint-weeks to land end-to-end (runtime + console surface). Dashboards mostly frontend work once metrics exist; instrumentation is the blocker.

jordan: For Dedicated/private customers we need a config toggle (opt-in) for sending trace metadata to the console. Also call out data residency/KMS concerns. Can we make the trace payload minimal?

anya: Good call. Plan: default = anonymized trace metadata (trace_id, span_durations, model_version). Full payload gated behind opt-in + consent flag. That should cover residency concerns.

matt d: Canary criteria proposed by SRE/product: - 72h stable canary window - P95 latency change vs baseline < +10% - request error rate delta <= +0.5 percentage points - token cost variance <= 5% - no unhandled fallback to CPU backends in the canary group

sofia: Sizing ask: need clear sample rates for traces. Suggest sample=1% globally, 10% for error traces, and 100% for canary cohort. Also need a lightweight span for model-selection so top-level trace size stays small.

customer-success: From customers: finance teams want a per-route cost export (CSV) and a breakdown by model-version. Also a way to tag routes with product-area so they can map spend.

anya: We can add export endpoint: `/api/v1/costs/export?start=&end=&tag=` returns CSV. On console side add a 'tagging' quickflow for routes. Low dev cost, high perceived value.

jordan: Deployment/rollout question — do we gate features behind a feature flag per-org? We should. For Dedicated we should ship as disabled and enable via account settings + docs.

matt d: Agreed. Feature flag per-org. Also need canary rollouts: 10% of traffic -> 30% -> 100% over 72h if criteria pass. Include automatic rollback.

sofia: Timeline/estimate: instrumentation + trace export endpoints = 2 sprints. Dashboards + CSV export UI = ~1 sprint. Feature flags + rollout automation = 1 sprint. Total = 4 sprints if we parallelize backend/frontend.

anya: Launch acceptance checklist (proposal): - Instrumentation landed and verified in staging - Dashboards populated with canonical sample data - Export CSV works and matches billing numbers within 1% - Canary automation + rollback tested in canary env - Docs + customer opt-in flow created - Security review for trace payloads completed

matt d: Prioritization notes: If we must cut scope for next ship, cut the long-tail error dashboard (keep overview + cost). Or cut full-trace payload opt-in and ship anonymized traces only. Which is less painful?

sofia: Cutting long-tail errors saves frontend time but pushes more work to post-launch triage. Cutting full-trace opt-in reduces compliance risk and shipping time. My recommendation: ship anonymized traces + long-tail errors in v2.

jordan: Ops ask: include a simple prometheus alert rule for canary failure. Example snippet:```yaml
- alert: CanaryRegression
  expr: (sum(rate(requests_total{job="canary"}[5m])) > 0) and (increase(errors_total{job="canary"}[15m]) / increase(requests_total{job="canary"}[15m]) > 0.005)
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Canary error rate > 0.5%"```

customer-success: Also capture UX for finance export — small modal to select date range, tags, and email results. Customers asked for scheduled exports monthly.

anya: Add scheduled exports to backlog as a stretch. Not required for v1.

matt d: OK next steps (owners): Sofia -> instrument traces + export endpoint (backend). Anya -> dashboard specs + console UI. Jordan -> feature flag + rollout automation + alerts. I'll own launch criteria, docs, and customer comms. We'll reconvene Thursday to finalize acceptance gates.

deploy-bot: deployment scheduled to staging: obs-instrumentation/feature-trace-hooks @ 2026-04-02T09:00:00Z :rocket:

sofia: noted. I'll post a staging demo link once the first traces show up.

matt d: Great — thanks everyone. If you have any hard objections to scope cuts, shout before EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
